analysis.title: What Matters Today: US Sharp Liquidation, Largest Move in Nasdaq VIX Since COVID, October Payrolls Preview (6 Nov 2026)
key_insights: Day one after the election saw AI underperform while the broader market rallied on a perceived pivot to the political center, led by quality, cyclicals and short covering. Day two was a sharp catch-down in the US market.

The author reads the speed and size of the moves as acute leverage and forced de-grossing. Correlations are rising, momentum is underperforming, the residual leverage factor is selling off, and low beta, safety and quality are bid.

The author leans toward a 1998-style liquidity event rather than March 2000. In 1998, Russia's default and LTCM were external shocks while US growth stayed intact, and markets recovered once liquidity returned and the Fed eased. The author says today's AI leaders have real revenues, cash flows and balance sheets, unlike 2000.

The author says delaying data centers does not destroy compute demand, and constrained capacity may improve existing economics. The parallel with 2000 is the scale of spending and the uncertainty about returns.

Four concerns underpin the AI selloff: insufficient capital to finance the buildout, insufficient revenue to justify the investment, insufficient power and permitting capacity to energize compute, and an unsustainable aggregate spending trajectory. The market has latched onto power and permitting, which the author calls arguably the least important. The open question is whether revenues justify the capital employed.
If data center construction slows sharply, nominal growth expectations look unrealistic, and the cyclicals that rallied on Wednesday look mispriced against that.

Negative gamma leaves scope for violent moves in either direction. The author thinks fundamental uncertainty justifies the de-rating, but the last leg overextended in a number of AI-related assets as forced de-risking became entrenched.
The author says what changes the narrative is political reflexivity around AI investment and growth, stabilization in funding markets, and evidence that spending and demand remain intact.

The author keeps the pre-election view that the S&P has been higher 12 months after each of the 19 midterms since 1950. This is a 12-month observation, not a one-month forecast. The author expects participants to play defense into the weekend, and says such episodes have historically been buying opportunities.

Hedge fund damage on the day: fundamental L/S -1.3% (-2 SD), US funds -1.7%, TMT funds down more than 4%, multi-strats -1.4% with momentum a 3.7 SD move. Systematic L/S held up at +0.2%. TMT managers are roughly flat YTD versus +24% before the summer AI unwind.

The VIX is at 27, which some clients called 'only' 27. The move was the largest 1-day change in Nasdaq's VIX since COVID, and levels are back near Liberation Day. In semis, the largest 1-day change in the VXSMH Index's history (data back to 2021).

The VIX had its second-largest 1-day move higher ever, behind only Volmageddon. Cboe saw more than 11mm puts trade, the largest put volume day on record, above the prior high in April 2025. Index puts led, and single-stock put activity was the fourth highest day ever.
Many GS AI-related baskets had their biggest down day since the launch of ChatGPT.

October payrolls preview: GS estimates nonfarm payrolls +75k, against consensus of +65k and a three-month average of +51k. Average hourly earnings are forecast at +0.3% m/m, in line with consensus, and unemployment is forecast unchanged at 4.2%, in line with consensus.

Arguments for a stronger payrolls report: initial jobless claims averaged 198k in the October payroll month versus 204k in September, alternative employment measures averaged about +70k, and October job growth has typically rebounded by an average of about 50k from the September pace due to residual seasonality.

sector_views.rationale: The author sees fundamental uncertainty justifying a de-rating but thinks the last leg of the selloff overextended. The author leans toward the AI growth engine remaining intact, provided demand, utilization and returns hold.
Cyclicals that rallied Wednesday look mispriced if data center construction slows sharply, because nominal growth expectations would be unrealistic.

tension_points.bull_case: The author leans toward 1998. AI leaders have real revenues, cash flows and balance sheets. Delaying data centers does not destroy compute demand, and constrained capacity may improve existing economics. The S&P has been higher 12 months after all 19 midterms since 1950.
tension_points.bear_case: The 2000 parallel is the scale of spending and uncertainty about returns, which could make this the start of a structural technology unwind. Fundamental uncertainty justifies the de-rating, and the cyclicals that rallied Wednesday look mispriced if data center construction slows dramatically.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Demand, utilization and returns failing to hold, per the author's condition that they 'need to hold'.

The largest 1-day change in Nasdaq's VIX since COVID and record put volume show broad-market protection demand.
